key_insight: Leverage vision-language models to generate human-like preference signals and use Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-style finetuning to align pretrained motion-forecasting / driving models with nuanced driving preferences.
problem_solved: Standard imitation objectives for large pretrained driving models often miss complex, context-dependent human driving preferences; VL-DPO addresses how to inject richer, commonsense preference information into finetuning without retraining from scratch.
method: Use vision-language models (VLMs) to interpret scenes and produce semantic preference signals or natural-language judgments about candidate driving behaviors.
Apply a DPO-style preference-alignment finetuning objective to pretrained motion-forecasting/autonomous driving models using the VLM-generated signals.
Preserve pretrained capabilities while adapting model outputs toward safer, more human-aligned trajectories with minimal extra annotation effort.
impact: Provides a practical pathway for practitioners to align autonomous driving behavior with human preferences using off-the-shelf VLMs, improving safety, interpretability, and customization without large-scale manual preference labeling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensor input → VLM reasoning (text/score) → DPO finetuning → aligned trajectory output

paper_title: VL-DPO: Vision-Language-Guided Finetuning for Preference-Aligned Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Zhefan Xu, Ghassen Jerfel, Marina Haliem, Qi Zhao, Jeonhyung Kang
